bug_description.normalized: The staged PKCS#12 witness is imported successfully and later parsed by gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse. When gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag examines the first AuthenticatedSafe entry, it stores the attacker-controlled inner contentType OID into stack buffer oid and then dispatches on it with strcmp(oid, DATA_OID). The witness encodes that inner OID as the one-byte DER object identifier 06 01 07, so libtasn1 materializes only the short dotted string prefix (for example "0.7" plus NUL) while the rest of oid's 128-byte stack storage remains uninitialized. MSAN reports that the resulting fixed-literal comparison reaches uninitialized bytes at offset 4 of a 21-byte read in __interceptor_memcmp. The staged fix metadata and patch bundle are unrelated to lib/x509/pkcs12.c and do not demonstrate the actual fix for this crash.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled DER witness and materializes it into the PKCS#12 ASN.1 tree later traversed by gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag.
source.value_from: The staged poc begins with a BER/DER PKCS#12 blob whose outer authSafe.contentType is the normal DATA_OID and whose authSafe.content contains an AuthenticatedSafe with first entry contentType bytes 06 01 07. Those bytes are preserved in pkcs12->pkcs12 and later re-read during bag extraction.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: oid is a stack buffer allocated without initialization. Only the bytes written by asn1_read_value for the current OID string become defined; the remaining tail stays poisoned until the strcmp sink reads it.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The contentType dispatch compares the partially initialized stack buffer oid against the 20-character DATA_OID literal, and the compare consumes uninitialized tail bytes from oid.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 4 inside a 21-byte read and attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of oid in gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag.

root_cause.description: The contentType dispatch buffer oid is stack-allocated without zero-initialization; asn1_read_value later fills only the short returned OID prefix, so the tail stays undefined when strcmp(oid, DATA_OID) reads it. Anchored at the declaration to match verified_invariants.root_cause_criterion (missing_initialization at line 608), tainted_value_origin, and the MSAN allocation attribution.
root_cause.note: gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag assumes oid is safe for a fixed-literal strcmp after asn1_read_value, but it never initializes the bytes beyond the returned OID string. For the witness the inner contentType (DER 06 01 07) decodes to a short dotted OID string, so asn1_read_value fills only that prefix and leaves oid's tail untouched; the later 21-byte strcmp(oid, DATA_OID) reaches those uninitialized bytes, which MSAN reports. A correct fix zero-initializes oid before the read (or avoids fixed-literal comparison that inspects bytes beyond the initialized prefix).

parser_admitted.condition: The witness imports as PKCS#12, _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe accepts the outer authSafe.contentType as DATA_OID, and simple_parse reaches the first bag extraction with idx == 0, so get_bag reads ?1.contentType from the attacker-controlled AuthenticatedSafe.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled PKCS#12 bytes and materializes them as the ASN.1 tree pkcs12->pkcs12. The staged witness includes an outer DATA_OID authSafe and inner AuthenticatedSafe bytes later traversed by gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag.
simple_parse starts its loop with idx == 0 and asks for the first bag from the imported PKCS#12 object, making the witness-controlled first AuthenticatedSafe entry reachable.

Allocates the stack buffer later used for contentType dispatch without initializing it. MSAN identifies this stack allocation in gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag as the origin of the poisoned bytes consumed at the sink.
Decodes the imported outer authSafe into ASN.1 tree c2 representing the inner AuthenticatedSafe. This makes the first entry's contentType available for direct readout from c2.

Reads ?1.contentType from c2 into oid after setting len to sizeof(oid) - 1. In the staged witness the first AuthenticatedSafe entry encodes contentType as DER 06 01 07, so libtasn1 writes only a short dotted string such as "0.7" plus NUL into oid; oid[4..127] remain uninitialized.

MSAN sink. Because step 5 returned ASN1_SUCCESS, the error exits are skipped and the code dispatches on oid. The compare against the 20-character DATA_OID literal reads 21 bytes in __interceptor_memcmp; with only the 4-byte "0.7\0" prefix initialized, the read reaches uninitialized bytes starting at offset 4 of oid.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of oid in the stack frame of gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag; the actual oid declaration is line 608.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is a PKCS#12 blob whose outer authSafe.contentType is the normal PKCS#7 DATA_OID, but whose first inner AuthenticatedSafe entry encodes contentType as the one-byte DER OBJECT IDENTIFIER 06 01 07. When gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse requests bag 0, gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag reads that short OID into stack buffer oid and then compares oid to DATA_OID, triggering MSAN on oid's uninitialized tail.

format.name: DER/BER PKCS#12 with malformed first inner contentType OID
format.contract: A PKCS#12 blob that imports successfully, reaches gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse bag index 0, and supplies an AuthenticatedSafe whose first entry contentType is encoded exactly as DER bytes 06 01 07 in the staged witness. That short OID causes asn1_read_value to initialize only a 4-byte dotted-string prefix in oid before strcmp(oid, DATA_OID) performs the 21-byte compare reported by MSAN. The verified trigger is this exact malformed inner contentType shape observed in the staged poc, not a generalized class of all invalid PKCS#12 files.
